Green — **29/29**. The `secrets` test now covers all three scenarios (grant/deny, output rejection, log masking).

## Slice 3 landed: log masking

- **`run_worker`** now masks every injected secret value out of the captured worker log before it goes anywhere — replaced with `[redacted secret]` (a marker naming no secret). This is the single chokepoint that covers the whole chain: the container's own stderr, runnerd's relay, and the server's failure message all derive from this one string, so scrubbing at the source scrubs all of them.
- Longest values first (so a secret containing another is masked whole), empty values skipped.
- Honestly labeled in the doc as best-effort / transform-blind — catches an accidental echo, not a determined exfiltrator (which the design already concedes is inside the trust boundary).
- New test: a worker that prints the secret then fails — the surfaced client-side log contains the redaction marker and **not** the raw value.

## Design status

- ✅ Out-of-band start-time injection, superset-match grants
- ✅ Hard output assertion at ingestion (slice 2)
- ✅ Best-effort log masking (this slice) — the leak-prevention trio is complete
- ⏳ **Tree-relative readers + `:@=` reader args** — full eval-path reader resolution (today only `std/<name>` readers resolve; others are skipped, never granting)

The whole design/secrets.md model is now working end-to-end except that grants can only name std tools. The remaining slice makes readers name repo-local tools too (resolved via eval-path, canonicalized against the job's tree revision) and support `:@=`/other arg modifiers in readers — the last gap between the implementation and the writeup. Want me to continue with that, or pause here?
